=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Buyer assessment

The Seller’s update leaves Wattlebridge exposed to several identified risks while seeking to restrict its remedies for them. The largest immediate concerns are **Bluefen consent**, **Riverlark repayment and security release**, the **$420,000 Completion bonuses**, and whether the Company owns the **Ironquay-developed IP**. The disclosure and liability provisions could then prevent recovery even if those matters cause loss.

The Seller describes many provisions as “standard,” cleared or agreed. The documents supplied do not establish that Wattlebridge accepted them, and the labels are not a substitute for reviewing their effect. Nor should the stated market ranges be accepted without independent support.

## Priority issues and proposed pushback

### 1. Bluefen: make effective consent a genuine Completion condition

Bluefen represents approximately **$3.6 million of FY26 revenue, or 30%**, and its contract contains a change-of-control consent mechanism with associated conditions. The Disclosure Letter says no final written consent or evidence of satisfaction of those conditions has been provided.

A promise to use “reasonable endeavours” is not equivalent to obtaining an effective, usable consent. Nor should delivery of a consent automatically satisfy the condition if it is conditional, qualified or requires further steps.

**Push for:**
- A condition precedent requiring Bluefen’s written consent to the transaction, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, and satisfaction or Buyer-approved waiver of all associated conditions before Completion.
- Prompt delivery of the full consent and related correspondence; no material adverse amendment or concession without Buyer approval.
- A long-stop date and Buyer termination right if the condition is not satisfied or waived. Only the Buyer should be able to waive a condition intended for its benefit.
- An interim covenant to preserve the Bluefen relationship.

**Immediate diligence:** Review DD-002 clauses 11.2–11.3 and seek Bluefen’s response. Do not assume consent will be withheld or that the change of control automatically terminates the contract.

### 2. Riverlark: repay and release security at Completion

The approximately **$3.2 million** Riverlark facility remains outstanding and no final security discharge is included. A release provided *after* Completion would expose the Buyer to buying a company with debt and security still in place, contrary to the **debt-free/cash-free** baseline.

**Push for:**
- A current payout statement, confirmation of all secured obligations and a binding discharge/release undertaking from Riverlark.
- A funds flow directing the required payout from the Seller’s Completion proceeds, with repayment and delivery of effective releases occurring simultaneously with Completion, including any required registrations and follow-up undertakings.
- Removal or release of any Company or group guarantees and security, as applicable.
- A price mechanism that deducts debt outstanding at Completion. Coordinate the direct bank payment and price adjustment so the same debt is **not deducted or paid twice**.

Review the facility’s change-of-control terms and confirm whether any separate consent or notice is required.

### 3. Completion bonuses: allocate the cost explicitly

DD-005 identifies **$420,000** in conditional Completion bonuses, absent from the draft funds flow. Their conditions include Completion and continued employment; payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. Calling them “a matter for the Seller” does not ensure that the Buyer is economically protected if the Company pays them after Completion.

**Push for:**
- Seller responsibility for the bonuses attributable to the sale, plus applicable employer on-costs.
- Express treatment in the purchase price/Completion accounts—such as a debt-like deduction—or a funded payment at Completion, with a specific indemnity for any residual exposure.
- Clear treatment of employees who do or do not satisfy the conditions and reconciliation of any amounts not ultimately payable. Avoid double recovery if an amount is already reflected in working capital, debt or another adjustment.

Obtain the bonus documents, employee status and payroll assessment before agreeing the amount.

### 4. Ironquay: secure ownership, not merely payment protection

DD-004 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows **$180,000 open**, but that is not independent proof of non-payment. The data room has neither a payment receipt nor a confirmatory assignment. The proposed indemnity limited to the particular SOW3 payment may not cover a title failure, infringement claim, remediation or disruption.

**Push for:**
- Before Completion, evidence that all SOW3 fees have cleared and an executed confirmation or assignment from Ironquay establishing the Company’s ownership or required rights, effective notwithstanding any historical payment issue.
- Review of the SOW and IP chain, including third-party components and any rights necessary to use, maintain and commercialise the materials.
- If the issue cannot be cured, a **specific indemnity** covering resulting claims, loss, defence costs and remediation—not just the open invoice—with an appropriate separate cap and survival period, outside general warranty thresholds and knowledge/disclosure defences.
- Consider a suitably sized escrow or retention if recovery against the Seller is uncertain.

### 5. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge: prevent a data-room dump from defeating claims

The Seller seeks to disclose the entire indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records, and to exclude claims for matters actually known **or merely discoverable** by the Buyer or its advisers. Together these provisions could shift unidentified risks to Wattlebridge and undermine the warranties it is paying for.

**Push for:**
- Delete blanket data-room/public-record disclosure and the “discoverable” knowledge exclusion.
- Permit disclosure against a warranty only where the matter is **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify its nature and scope**, through a specific reference to an identified document or extract, with context reasonably necessary to assess it.
- Limit any knowledge qualifier to actual knowledge of specifically named Buyer individuals, without imputation of advisers’ knowledge or a duty of inquiry.
- Ensure disclosure and knowledge do not defeat specific indemnities, price adjustments, Completion obligations or claims involving fraud, subject to applicable law.
- Obtain a fixed, complete data-room index and preserved copy of the disclosed materials.

A disclosure is not proof that an adverse conclusion is true. For example, the incident is not established as a confirmed breach, and the Ironquay ledger is not proof that the invoice is unpaid. But the disclosures identify risks that need resolution or explicit allocation.

### 6. Liability package: separate fundamental and specific risks from general warranties

The proposed general warranty cap is **$4.8 million**, the de minimis is **$25,000**, and the **$250,000 deductible basket** allows recovery only of the excess. General claims must be notified within **18 months**. Most concerningly, the Seller proposes extending limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to claims of every nature, while putting title and capacity under the same regime.

**Push for:**
- A materially stronger general warranty package: negotiate the cap and survival period in light of diligence and available recourse; reduce the thresholds and seek a **tipping basket** rather than an excess-only basket. Ensure qualifying related claims can be aggregated and the notice standard is workable.
- Separate **fundamental warranties**, including title, capacity and authority, with a cap up to the purchase price, no de minimis or basket, and a longer survival period.
- Separate treatment for **tax**: a specific tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax liabilities, appropriate longer survival linked to relevant assessment periods, and clear allocation through the price mechanics.
- Appropriate protection for material **IP** warranties and the identified Ironquay exposure, rather than assuming the general package is sufficient.
- Expressly preserve claims for debt and price adjustments, specific indemnities, breaches of Completion and other covenants, and available equitable relief. Carve out fraud and other liability that cannot lawfully be excluded or restricted; have NSW counsel check the precise drafting and statutory position.
- Review the interaction of the cap, exclusive-remedy, non-reliance, disclosure and knowledge clauses across the entire SPA. Labels alone will not prevent an unintended limitation.

### 7. Export/privacy incident: investigate and allocate the known risk

A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain approximately **1,240 records**, but access, scope, notification requirements and loss remain unknown. Neither “preliminary” nor “not expected to be material” resolves the risk.

**Push for:**
- Prompt preservation and delivery of logs, forensic findings, correspondence and the incident response; ascertain access, recipients, data contents, containment and deletion.
- Assessment by privacy counsel of applicable notification and other obligations, including under the Australian notifiable data breaches regime where applicable; do not assume notification is or is not required.
- A Seller-funded, specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident-related investigation, notification, remediation, claims and regulatory costs to the extent legally recoverable, with appropriate conduct/cooperation provisions and protection outside the general warranty limitations.
- Consider a retention or escrow pending investigation if exposure remains uncertain at Completion.

### 8. Supplier renewals: determine whether they affect price or operating forecasts

The three related renewals total **$330,000**. The supplied material does not establish that they are unavoidable, accrued, terminable or ordinary-course costs. Conversely, their existence alone does not establish that all $330,000 is debt or an additional loss.

**Push for:** Review DD-008 and DD-011 together, including timing, cancellation rights, services received and accounting treatment. Include any properly attributable pre-Completion liability or non-ordinary-course commitment in the agreed adjustment or seek a targeted remedy. Avoid counting an ordinary post-Completion operating expense twice.

### 9. Title and remaining contract points

- **Share title:** DD-012 is evidence that Harbourglass is recorded as holder of all issued shares; it is not complete independent verification of title, encumbrances or the capital structure. Obtain constitutional and statutory records, searches and evidence of any releases; require executed transfers, corporate approvals and registration steps at Completion. Back these with fundamental warranties.
- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a **notification**, not a stated consent requirement. Check its timing and ensure the responsible party gives any required notice.
- **Mossvale:** DD-009 restricts **assignment**; it does not, on the supplied facts, say a share sale requires consent. Review the full contract and transaction structure before requesting one.

## Recommended negotiation sequence

1. **Make Completion conditional on effective Bluefen consent and simultaneous Riverlark repayment and release.**
2. **Correct the funds flow and price mechanics** for Riverlark and the bonuses, including on-costs and anti-double-counting provisions.
3. **Cure Ironquay IP title and investigate the export incident**; use specific indemnities and, where justified, escrow for unresolved exposure.
4. **Reject blanket disclosure, discoverability and all-claims limitations.** Separate fundamental, tax, IP and specific-indemnity protection from the general warranty regime.
5. Complete targeted diligence on supplier renewals, title, notices and the full underlying contracts before accepting the Seller’s characterisations.
